label: Aquinas, De ente Cap.3: a thing that is its own esse can only be one
locator: cap.3 [69874]: Unde relinquitur quod talis res, quae sit suum esse, non potest esse nisi una
interpretation: Baur/Koch c.3 (Leonine c.4). It remains that such a thing, which is its own esse, cannot be but one. Read as 'at most one': any two beings in act whose represented esse equals their essence are the same. The sentence does not assert that such a thing exists (the passage introduces it with 'nisi forte sit aliqua res'); the restriction to beings in act weakens it. The passage's reason is the multiplication inventory and the exclusion of difference and matter; the premise that two such things would share one nature is the analyst's.
attribution: The passage states that a thing which is its own esse cannot be but one, which is the premise (read as at most one, among beings in act).
